title: Burler: no cluster-exclude warning when the profile has no cluster fan
brief: Every Burler round WARNs about dropped cluster excludes; fix at the source (#278)
body:
Repro: any loom run; every Burler round logs `shedadapters: focus directive names cluster excludes but the template profile has no cluster fan; dropping` (WARN).
Impact: the judge writes an `exclude_lenses` list nothing consumes, and the WARN buries real warnings in traces.

Found in crucible-happy-path round fable-high-r2.

Source: https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/278
Preferred fix: stop asking the Burler judge for exclude_lenses (and stop warning) when the template profile has no cluster fan, rather than only downgrading the log level.

title: lyx loom start pane layout: small status band, no loom-operator, agent gets the height
brief: lyx loom start pane layout (#279)
body:
Observed on the first real `lyx loom start` (go driver, task `burler-exclude-warn` in a loomyard hub), the task's tmux window holds four panes, top to bottom:

1. `lyx loom status --watch` — takes about a third of the window height (and half of it under `--no-attach`, where there is no `loom-operator` pane). **Must be small: a few rows at most, just enough to show what the run is doing.** It is an overview, never a peer of the agent pane.
2. `loom-operator`: an empty bash that `lyx loom start` adds (`operatorStrandAddSpec`, `internal/loomcli/bootstrap.go`, anchored `AnchorBelowParent`, so it lands directly under the status pane). **Must not exist.**
3. The agent pane — each producer's agent under the go driver, or the ly-drive session under the llm driver. **Must take all remaining height.**
4. **Selvage**, reed's permanent one-line shell band at the bottom (`internal/reedengine`, `selvagepane.go`). **This is exactly the operator terminal wanted** — keep it as is.

Wanted layout, top to bottom: a small status band, the agent pane filling everything else, Selvage.

## Why there are two operator shells

Both landed on 2026-09-19 from parallel work that was never reconciled: `d39b30648` replaced reed's header pane with a status line and Selvage, and `8ca2b9dbf` ("reed: born-as-strand for loom start's operator attach") added `loom-operator` as a separate tracked strand for the operator to attach in.
Selvage already is the operator's terminal, so `loom-operator` only duplicates it.

## Fix

- Stop adding `loom-operator`. If born-as-strand's tracking of the operator's pane is still needed (addressing, e.g. the mailbox design), make Selvage that tracked pane rather than adding another.
- Pin the status strand to a small fixed height.
- Size the agent pane to the rest, under both drivers.

Source: https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/279 (close it in the landing commit).

title: loom status shows the producer's stuck reason, not 'stuck with no OnStuck target'
brief: loom status shows the producer's stuck reason, not 'stuck with no OnStuck target'
body:
On the first real `lyx loom start` (task `burler-exclude-warn`, landing in PR mode), Publish created PR #280 and stopped to wait for review, which is correct. The status strand showed:

```
loom blocked | now Publish | last Publish → stuck | wait stuck with no OnStuck target
```

`stuck with no OnStuck target` is shed wiring jargon: it says how the recipe is connected, not what the run is doing. The producer's own reason was available — the trace carries `landingshed: producer stuck producer=Publish reason="pull request created; awaiting review"` and `landingshed: pull request created number=280` — but it never reaches `wait` in the status line or `error` in `lyx loom status`.

Wanted: when a row ends stuck with no OnStuck target, `wait` and `error` carry the producer's own stuck reason; Publish's reason includes the PR URL, e.g.

```
loom blocked | now Publish | last Publish → stuck | wait pull request created; awaiting review: https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/pull/280
```

This is the crucible-happy-path F7 residual ("the cause of a blocked row is visible only in the trace file"), now hit on a real run.

Source: https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/283 (close it in the landing commit).

title: Plan verify: code-fence lines are not commands
brief: Strip code fences from the plan-level verify command (#285)
body:
On the first real lyx loom run (task `burler-exclude-warn`, PR #280), Webster's integration fork reported that the verify command in its rendered prompt `integration.md` was mangled by nested code fences, so it ran the plan's own `## verify:` command from `00-overview.md` instead.

The fork recovered by itself, but the integration stage's prompt carries the one command that decides whether the whole plan passes: a fork that trusts the rendered text runs something other than the plan's verify, and one that cannot recover it fails the stage.

Expected: the verify command renders into `integration.md` verbatim and unambiguous, whatever fences the plan's command or its surrounding prompt text use (e.g. a fence longer than any backtick run inside the command, or the command outside a fenced block).

## Second occurrence

Second occurrence, and it is wider than `integration.md`'s rendering. On the `stuck-reason-in-status` run (llm driver), the plan put its `## verify:` command inside a ```bash fence, and Webster ran the fence lines as part of the command:

```
websterengine: verify command exited verifyCmd="```bash && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... && go test -tags integration ./... && ```" exitCode=2
```

The plan-level verify is joined line by line with `&&` fence markers included, so the shell fails on syntax (exit 2) at every commit. That also makes the integration stage's SHA-bisect useless: every candidate fails the same way, so it can never localize the commit that actually broke (here a real test failure was masked this way).

Fix belongs where `plan.Verify` is extracted (planparser), not only in the prompt render: strip a fenced block's markers, or reject a fenced verify section at the plan gate so the planner rewrites it.

## Where the fix goes

`internal/planparser/sections.go`, `joinVerifyCommands`: skip markdown code-fence lines (a trimmed line starting with ``````` or `~~~`, with or without a language name) when chaining the section's lines, so a fenced `## verify:` yields the same command as a bare one.
Add fenced cases (with language, bare, tilde, fence-only) to `TestParsePlan_VerifySection_ChainsEveryLine` in `sections_test.go`, and state the rule in `contracts/specs/loom-plan-spec.md` next to "the parser chains every non-blank line".

## Constraint for this run

The deployed lyx still has this bug, so this plan's own `## verify:` section MUST be one plain command line with no code fences, or this run blocks on it exactly like `stuck-reason-in-status` did.

Source: https://github.com/Knatte18/loomyard/issues/285 (close it in the landing commit).

title: Landing: board status, PR body, squash message, operator-approved merge, branch cleanup
body:
Landing gaps, one task. Read each issue in full; they are the spec.

- #275: a landed run leaves its board task open; Finalize should mark it `done`.
- #276: the landing squash message is Webster's whole `summary.md`, including false fork warnings.
- #289: the Publish PR body is Webster's run narrative instead of a description of the change.
- #292: an operator approval lets Publish proceed without a GitHub merge; Finalize squash-merges locally with exactly one `Co-Authored-By` trailer and closes the PR.
- #293: `lyx fabric remove` leaves the local warp branch behind.

#276, #289 and #292 share one root: `summary.md` is a run record, not a change description. Decide one source for the PR body and the squash message.

title: Operator surface: what the operator sees and types while a run goes
brief: Operator surface: #295, #277, #286, #297 + four unfiled findings
body:
Read the closed GitHub issues #295, #277, #286 and #297 (all folded here), plus these findings that were never filed:

- **Status is unreadable.** `lyx loom status` gives raw JSON; `stuck` means both normal Bouncer-to-Burler routing and a real failure; nothing says how far the run has come (which segment of the recipe, what is left). The operator cannot follow a run without reading traces.
- **A deploy does not upgrade running sessions.** `lyx loom start` finds the existing status strand via `IfAbsent` and keeps its old display after `update-plugins.sh`.
- **Layout rule.** Every pane but the bottom-most collapses to a fixed configurable minimum (3 rows) and the bottom-most takes the rest; adding a pane moves nothing above it (`3+20` becomes `3+3+17`). Selvage is excluded.
- **ly-drive reporting.** Name the run by its slug, never `self`; give the run's own history position, not ly-drive's step counter; say when a reported state is from before it acted. `_lyx/shed/self/` should be named by slug, with `self` only an alias.- **`lyx fabric remove` hides the warp-branch outcome.** `internal/fabriccli/fabric.go` builds its output map by hand and never added `WarpBranchDeleted`/`WarpBranchKeptReason` from landing (#298); a kept branch is silent, although the help text promises `warp_branch_kept_reason`.
- **README recipe is stale.** `README.md` still lists `Webster-Review → Publish → Finalize`, without `Describe`.
- **`blocked` is the wrong word for a ready PR.** A run waiting on PR review by design reads as `blocked`, the same word as a real failure. Give the planned hand-off its own state (e.g. `awaiting-review`) in `status.json`, `loom status` and ly-drive reports.
- **ly-drive step commands are long boilerplate.** Each step hand-builds a trace id, redirects stdout/stderr to scratch files and cats them back. `lyx shed step` should mint the trace id and keep its own output, so the agent runs just `lyx shed step <slug>`.

#286 replaces the old board entry `stencil-drift-remedy`.

title: Burler review rounds: tracked records, focus steering, directive precedence
brief: Burler: #287, #282, #263 + comment-width finding
body:
Read the closed GitHub issues #287, #282 and #263 (all folded here), plus this finding that was never filed:

- **Comment width is unwritten.** The 100-column comment width, and how a leading tab counts toward it, is written down nowhere, so a width finding costs a whole review round (friction note `burler-webster-r2.md` from the `stuck-reason-in-status` run).
- **Plan verify misses touched packages.** The `landing` plan's `## verify:` integration line named four packages; card 20's `//go:build integration` test in `internal/websterengine` failed unnoticed until Burler ran the tag over every touched package (friction note `burler-webster-r1.md` from `landing`). Plan review should check that verify covers every package a card touches.

title: batten opens VS Code on the new pair with reed attached
brief: Batten lifecycle step: open a VS Code window whose terminal is attached to the child run
body:
Goal: when batten starts a task, a VS Code window opens on the new pair with the child run's reed session already attached in its terminal, so the operator watches the run without typing any command.

Batten owns the task worktree's lifecycle (`contracts/recipes/batten-recipe.yaml`: `Worktree-Create` -> `Seed-Child` -> `Run-Shed` -> `Worktree-Teardown`); opening the IDE is a lifecycle step, not part of the loom run.

Today:
- Nothing opens a window; the operator runs `cd <hub>/<slug> && lyx reed attach` by hand.
- `lyx ide spawn <slug>` (`internal/ideengine/spawn.go`, `internal/vscode/config.go`) writes `.vscode/settings.json` and `tasks.json` only when absent, and its `folderOpen` chain is `reed up` -> `reed add claude` -> `reed attach`.
  For a driven pair that chain is wrong: it adds a second, bare claude strand next to the ly-drive strand.

Wanted:
- A batten producer after the child's driver strand is up opens VS Code on the pair through `ideengine`.
- The generated `folderOpen` task for a driven pair runs `lyx reed attach` only — no `reed up`, no `reed add claude`.
- Launch failure (no `code` on PATH, headless machine) degrades to a warning; the lifecycle continues.

Open: where the strand-is-up point lies (batten's `Run-Shed` starts the child's driver, or `Seed-Child` does), and whether an existing `tasks.json` from a plain `ide spawn` is rewritten.

title: Batten ready for the hub loop: wait through awaiting, keep run records
brief: Batten keeps watching an awaiting child, run records survive teardown, approval time off the watch budget
body:
Goal: the hub orchestrator drives every task with `lyx batten run <slug>` from the prime instead of hand-running `fabric add`, `loom start --no-attach` and `fabric remove`.
Three gaps block that today.

1. **An awaiting child is a planned hand-off, not a halt.**
   After `operator-surface`, a child waiting at Publish for PR approval is `awaiting`; its card 13 makes batten's `Run-Shed` (`internal/battenshed#innerRunProducer.Call`) hard-error on it, failing the batten run and adding a third manual resume.
   Wanted: `Run-Shed` keeps watching an `awaiting` child (self-route, like `running`), so the flow is batten in the background -> orchestrator reviews and runs `lyx loom approve` -> child re-stepped -> batten sees `done` -> `Worktree-Teardown`.
   `blocked`, `failed` and `paused` stay halts.
2. **Teardown destroys the run's records.**
   Friction notes (`loomengine.LoomFrictionDir`, under `.lyx/loom/friction/`) and the driver report (`internal/loomcli/driverreport.go`, under `.lyx/shed/self/`) are machine-local scratch and vanish with the pair.
   Wanted: both live under `_lyx/` and are committed by Go at a loom boundary (same route as `_lyx/reviews/`, `loomcli#statusCommitPathspec`), so they survive teardown on the pushed weft branch.
3. **The watch budget counts approval time.**
   `Run-Shed` has `max_bounces: 1440` at `poll_interval_s: 30` (12 h, `contracts/recipes/batten-recipe.yaml`); a PR left for approval overnight exhausts it.
   Wanted: time spent `awaiting` does not consume the budget (or has its own, much larger one).

Out of scope: deploy (stays with the hub prime after landing); opening VS Code (`batten-open-ide`).

title: ide: hub workspace with prime, board and portals
brief: One generated VS Code workspace shows the board beside the prime
body:
The operator wants to watch the board (and running tasks) in VS Code while talking to the hub orchestrator in the prime.
Direction: `lyx ide spawn` for the prime generates `<hub>/_launchers/<prime>.code-workspace` with folders prime, `_board` and `_portals`, and opens that instead of the bare folder.
Lyx-owned, outside every worktree, so agents never see it; task windows stay one pair each.
`code --add` works today but is ad hoc.

title: Publish: verify the tree after merging the parent
brief: A conflict-resolved parent merge was pushed with non-compiling tests
body:
Publish merges the parent into the task branch and pushes without compiling or testing the result.
In run `operator-surface` (PR #300) the conflict-resolved merge `854eb73fe` left four test call sites on the old `shedrun.StatusRel(runID)` signature (`internal/loomcli/wiring_commitstatus_test.go`, `..._integration_test.go`), so `go vet`/`go test` failed while `go build` passed; only the hub's PR review caught it.
Fix direction: after a parent merge that changed the tree, Publish runs the plan's `## verify:` command (or at least `go vet ./...` across build tags) and halts stuck on failure before pushing and opening or updating the PR.

title: Webster fork audit: text search for "lyx fabric" counted as a fabric operation
brief: RefScanner flags quoted grep patterns; a done batch cannot be recorded
body:
`fabricengine.RefScanner` (`internal/fabricengine/refscanner.go`) flags any Bash command whose text matches `lyx(\.exe)?\s+(fabric|weft|warp)\b`, including a quoted search pattern.
Run `operator-surface` blocked at Webster batch 28 (docs card, commit `d369f8915`, report OK) because the fork ran `grep -n "fabric remove\|lyx fabric.*remove" docs/overview.md` — a content search in the warp, not a fabric operation.
The flagged transcript never enters `seenForkTranscripts`, so every retry of `record-batch 28` re-audits it and fails again: the run cannot resume without a code change.
Fix direction: match `lyx fabric|weft|warp` only in command position (start of the command or after `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `$(`), not inside quoted arguments; keep the weft-path match.
Docs cards will keep hitting this, since docs describe fabric verbs.

Fixed for the spelling in `777d93af7` (hub prime, deployed): command position only, quoted spans blanked.
Still open: the path half (`\S*-weft\b`) matches any word ending in `-weft`, quoted or not, so a docs grep for `main-weft` would trip the same dead end.

Path half fixed in `b848b8f9f` (hub prime, deployed): heredoc bodies dropped, a weft sibling counts as a path only after a separator, a bare `-weft` word only outside quotes. Triggered by run `batten-hub-ready` batch 11 (a fork writing `archive_integration_test.go` via heredoc).

title: Plan-Write: respawn archives the finished plan; Agent refusal unannounced
brief: Respawn starts over instead of reusing the plan; prompt does not say Agent is refused
body:
Friction from run `operator-surface` (Plan-Write, trace `7b2a74344919ecc3`).
1. A respawned Plan-Write moves an existing finished plan to `_lyx/plan/archive-<ts>/` and starts from an empty directory; the new session learned of the prior plan only from a cross-session message.
   The false `asking` that caused the respawn is fixed in `083e992cf`, but any respawn still discards the plan: a respawn should reuse or at least point the prompt at the archived cards.
2. A PreToolUse hook refuses the Agent tool in the Plan-Write pane and the prompt does not say so; five parallel explorer dispatches failed before work started.
   The prompt should state the tool restriction (see Someday "shuttle `Spec`: generic tools-restriction").

title: Trace logs: configurable retention, fewer files from routine commands
brief: Trace logs: configurable retention, fewer files from routine commands
body:
`.lyx/logs` gets one trace file per lyx invocation that logs at INFO+ or exits non-zero (`internal/logger/sink.go`); `internal/logger/retention.go` keeps the newest 50 files and nothing older than 14 days, both hard-coded.
Operator board upserts and fabric verbs fill the 50 slots, pushing a run's interesting traces out.
Options: make both bounds config keys; or arm the sink only on failure or when a trace id is set (loom runs, ly-drive steps).
Observed in run `operator-surface`: the Webster step's own live trace was swept by retention before the step returned, so the driver's `trace_file` pointed at a missing file.
Retention must never delete the trace of a still-running invocation (skip files held by a live pid, or sweep only at process exit).

title: lyx quarry: per-glyph resolve answers, grep-safe glyphs output
brief: lyx quarry: per-glyph resolve answers, grep-safe glyphs output
body:
- **One bad glyph sinks the whole `resolve` batch.** `lyx quarry resolve a b bad` returns only `{"error":"<bad>: not_found","ok":false}`, nothing for the valid glyphs. quarry itself answers per glyph; `internal/quarrycli/resolve.go` collects every non-found status and fails the whole invocation by design. A planner checking spellings wants one answer per glyph, with the bad one marked `not_found`.
- **`glyphs` output invites a broken grep.** A Plan-Write agent ran `lyx quarry glyphs internal/shedengine | grep -v "_test"` to drop test symbols; the JSON is pretty-printed one field per line, so the grep removed only each test symbol's `"file": ..._test.go` line and left the symbol without `file` (quarry#33, closed: quarry is correct). Give `lyx quarry glyphs` a flag that excludes test-file symbols, or emit one symbol per line, so the obvious filter is either unnecessary or correct.

Reported by the `operator-surface` Plan-Write session (2026-09-30).

title: Burler: warn when the explore stencil lacks the focus_directive marker
brief: Burler: warn when the explore stencil lacks the focus_directive marker
body: `internal/burlerengine/prompt.go`: friction warns when its stencil marker is missing (`friction.WarnIfMarkerAbsent`), but `{{.focus_directive}}` has no such check. Since #299 the focus directive no longer also rides `PriorReviews`, so a board explore stencil without the marker (dev build, operator-edited board copy) silently drops the Bouncer's focus from every Burler round. Add the same warning. Found in the #299 review.

title: reed: send a short launch-script line instead of the full command
brief: Hide the long env+claude launch line behind a generated launch script
body:
Every strand pane shows a long typed launch line before the agent starts: the pane-binary prelude (`export PATH=…`, `export LYX_BIN=…`, `internal/reedengine/panebin.go`) chained onto the claude invocation (`CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=1`, `"$(cat prompt.md)"`, `--session-id`, `--settings`, `--model`, `--effort`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, `internal/shuttleengine/claudeengine/command.go`), sent with `send-keys` into an interactive shell.
The operator finds it noisy.
Direction: reed writes the composed line to a `launch.sh` (or `.ps1`) in the strand's scratch dir and sends only `. <path>/launch.sh`; behaviour unchanged, the full line stays inspectable in the file.

title: One driving surface per run: ly-drive pane or status strand, never both
brief: llm-driven run shows only ly-drive; go-driven run shows only the status strand
body:
Operator decision: a run's tmux session shows exactly one driving surface, chosen by the run's driver.
- `llm` driver: only the ly-drive session pane; no loom-status strand (the driver already reports progress, the status band above it is noise).
- `go` driver: only the loom-status strand.

Today `lyx loom start` always ensures the status strand (`internal/loomcli/arm.go` calls `ensureStatusStrand`, `internal/loomcli/sharedbootstrap.go`), and an llm-driven run adds the ly-drive strand next to it.
Wanted: `ensureStatusStrand` runs only for a `go`-driven run (driver read from the run's seed), and a resume of an llm run whose session still holds a status strand from an older build removes it.
`lyx loom status` stays available as a command either way.
Driver pane height needs no new key: with the status strand gone, the stack is ly-drive over the agent, so `collapsed_rows` is the ly-drive height (hub config set to 16 in weft `main-weft`).

title: fabric add after remove: leftover remote weft branch rejects the push (flaky test)
brief: Re-adding a removed slug races the old remote weft branch; integration test flakes
body:
`TestRemove_AddSucceedsAfterWarpBranchDeleted` (`internal/fabricengine/remove_warpbranch_integration_test.go`) is flaky: run `ide-hub-workspace` failed its plan verify with "push of wb-readd-weft rejected non-fast-forward"; the same test passes on reruns on main and in the task worktree.
The test adds `wb-readd`, removes it without `--remote` (the pushed weft branch stays on the fixture's origin), then adds it again: the re-created weft branch pushes only if it happens to match or fast-forward the old remote one, which depends on commit timestamps.
This is a product gap too: `lyx fabric add <slug>` after a plain `fabric remove <slug>` can fail on the leftover remote weft branch.
Fix direction: Add adopts or resets an orphaned remote weft branch of the same name (or Remove records it and Add refuses with a remedy), and the test pins that deterministically.

Hit twice in a row in run `ide-hub-workspace` (integration verify, then again after re-step); both times the verify passed when rerun by hand.
Likely mechanism: the re-created weft branch's bootstrap commits are identical to the old ones only when they land in the same second (same SHA, push is a no-op); otherwise they diverge and the push is rejected, so in real use a re-add of a removed slug nearly always fails.
The integration verify report (`_lyx/webster/reports/integration.yaml`) carries only `status: FAILED`, no failing test name or output; the hub had to dig the fork transcript for it.

title: Webster verify: rerun, compare with parent, halt only on a real regression
brief: Flaky or pre-existing test failures no longer halt a run; report names the failing tests
body:
A red plan verify halts the whole run at Webster, whatever the cause.
Run `ide-hub-workspace` blocked twice on the flaky `TestRemove_AddSucceedsAfterWarpBranchDeleted` (see `fabric-readd-weft-push`), in a package the task did not break; the verify was green when rerun by hand.

Wanted, when the integration verify fails:
1. Rerun the failing tests once. Green on rerun: continue, and record the test as flaky in the run's report and friction.
2. Still red: run the same tests at the parent commit. Red there too: continue with a pre-existing-failure warning.
3. Halt only when a test fails on the task head and passes on the parent (a real regression).

Also: the integration report (`_lyx/webster/reports/integration.yaml`, `contracts/stencils/webster/webster-template-integration.md`) records only `status: OK | FAILED`; it must carry the failing test names and the tail of their output, so neither the driver nor the hub has to dig the fork transcript.

title: Webster: a parent merge after a batch commit wedges record-batch
brief: record-batch demands HEAD == report head_sha; a mid-run merge-in wedges the run
body:
Webster has no path for a batch whose fork committed and reported OK when HEAD has since moved by a parent merge (run `batten-hub-ready`, batch 11, after the hub ran `lyx fabric merge-in main` to pick up a deployed fix).
`record-batch` refuses on report `head_sha` != worktree HEAD, and `begin-batch`/`recover-batch` refuse because an OK report exists: the run is wedged until the merge is removed (the hub reset the unpushed merge commit).
Also found: a batch left non-terminal after a refused record-batch wedged resume on create-already-exists; fixed in `b16efae35` and `4ab6f6dd6` (`begunCards`).
Fix direction: record-batch accepts a HEAD whose first-parent chain reaches the report's `head_sha` through merge commits only; and loom/fabric warn against a parent merge while Webster is mid-run.

title: Every refusal has a way forward: audit Webster and shed halt paths
brief: Walk every refusal/halt path in webster and shed; none may wedge a run
body:
Principle (operator-agreed): a false stop is as serious as a wrong landing; every refusal lyx issues must leave a documented way forward, and a guard that does not protect correctness warns and records instead of halting.

Evidence from 2026-09-30 (runs `operator-surface`, `batten-hub-ready`, `ide-hub-workspace`), each needing a hub code fix and deploy to continue:
- fork-audit false positives made a done batch unrecordable forever (flagged transcript never enters `seenForkTranscripts`) — `777d93af7`, `b848b8f9f`;
- run-entry and begin-batch validation refused a begun-but-unrecorded batch as create-already-exists — `b16efae35`, `4ab6f6dd6`;
- record-batch / begin-batch / recover-batch refuse each other in a ring after a parent merge (`webster-parent-merge-midrun`).

Scope: enumerate every refusal in `internal/websterengine`, `internal/webstercli`, `internal/shedengine`, `internal/loomcli` (preflight, coherence, fingerprint, audit, head-SHA, report-exists gates). For each: can a run reach it through no fault of its own? Is there a verb or state transition out of it? Is the halt needed for correctness, or can it warn?
Deliver: a table in the webster module doc (refusal, trigger, way forward), fixes for every refusal without a way forward, and tests reaching each from a realistic state.
Policy-class audit findings (fabric-reference, named spawn) on a batch whose report is OK and whose commits pass verify become recorded warnings, not halts.

title: ly-drive: safe self-repairs instead of always handing back
brief: Driver re-steps known transient stops itself; hands back only real decisions
body:
Today the ly-drive skill never repairs a blocked run: it writes a report, hands back and exits, and every recovery is done by the hub by hand (a message the operator must also approve in the pane, since the driver runs in bypass mode).
On 2026-09-30 most hand-backs were transient or false stops that a single re-step after the underlying fix would have cleared.

Wanted:
- A closed list of safe repairs the driver may do on its own, each recorded under `<scratch>/repairs/`: one re-step of a stop whose reason matches a known-transient class (flaky verify once `verify-triage` exists, a verb that failed on infrastructure), and a re-step after the lyx binary changed since the stop (a deploy landed a fix).
- Everything else still hands back; `awaiting` at Publish is the operator's hand-off, never auto-approved.
- The driver stays alive after a hand-back (waits for a resume message) instead of exiting, so the hub resumes it with one message rather than `lyx loom start` spawning a fresh session.

title: Hub orchestrator as a reed strand with automatic handoff
brief: lyx hosts the hub orchestrator in tmux and cycles its context via handoff
body:
The hub orchestrator's context fills over a long day; compaction loses detail, and the manual remedy is `/scribe:handoff` then a fresh session.
Proposal: `lyx hub orch` (name open) runs the orchestrator as an interactive claude strand in its own reed session, and a watcher cycles it:
1. Read context usage from the session transcript (usage fields) after each turn.
2. Above a threshold, when the session is idle (shuttle's idle/asking classification), inject `/scribe:handoff <path>` and wait for the file.
3. Inject `/clear`, then a resume prompt that reads the handoff and the board.
Durable state already lives outside the context (board queue and dependencies, run status files, drive reports, `manifest/HANDOFF.md`), so a fresh session loses little.
The operator talks to the orchestrator through `lyx reed attach` or the hub VS Code workspace terminal.
Open: threshold, whether the operator's own terminal session can be adopted instead of spawning a new one, and cross-session messaging to a strand-hosted orchestrator.
